webhooks.summary: Mercury provides a full webhook management API (list, create, get, update, delete, and verify) under `/webhooks`. The formal `webhookEventNames` collection in the provided OpenAPI content is empty, but the `verifyWebhook` operation description explicitly references event types `transaction.created` and `transaction.updated` as examples. No signature headers or payload-signing verification scheme are documented in the supplied material; the only verification mechanism described is an outbound test-event ping to the registered endpoint.

events.name: transaction.created
events.description: Referenced as an example event type in the verifyWebhook operation (POST /webhooks/{webhookEndpointId}/verify). Default test event when no eventType is supplied.

events.name: transaction.updated
events.description: Referenced as an example event type in the verifyWebhook operation (POST /webhooks/{webhookEndpointId}/verify).

managementEndpoints.description: Retrieve a paginated list of all webhook endpoints for your organization. Supports filtering by status.
Register a new webhook endpoint to receive event notifications.
Retrieve details of a specific webhook endpoint by ID.
Update the configuration of an existing webhook endpoint. A webhook disabled due to consecutive delivery failures can be reactivated by setting status to 'active'.

Send a test event to verify the webhook endpoint is properly configured and reachable. Optional 'eventType' field in the body specifies the test event type; defaults to 'transaction.created' when omitted.

signature.detail: No signature header or HMAC/secret-based payload verification scheme is described in the provided OpenAPI content. The only 'verify' capability is an outbound test event sent to the registered endpoint via POST /webhooks/{webhookEndpointId}/verify — this validates endpoint reachability, not payload authenticity.

setupSteps.title: Obtain the inbound hook URL from the registry
setupSteps.detail: In the package registry, open the webhooks area for the target workspace and copy the stable inbound hook URL exposed for Mercury integrations. This URL is where Mercury will POST event notifications.

setupSteps.title: Register the hook URL with Mercury
setupSteps.detail: Call POST /webhooks with the inbound hook URL as the target endpoint so Mercury begins delivering event notifications to the registry. Confirm the creation via GET /webhooks and capture the returned webhookEndpointId.

setupSteps.title: Verify endpoint reachability
setupSteps.detail: Call POST /webhooks/{webhookEndpointId}/verify, optionally specifying an 'eventType' (e.g., 'transaction.created' or 'transaction.updated'); if omitted it defaults to 'transaction.created'. Confirm a successful test delivery in the registry webhook area.

setupSteps.title: Register the hook URL in the registry webhooks area
setupSteps.detail: Finalize the integration by saving the Mercury webhook configuration (provider, endpoint ID, and any event filters) in the registry's webhooks area so inbound Mercury events trigger the intended workspace workflow.
